page.content:
Highland species behind most specialty and traditional café coffee.

How Coffea arabica connects

  • Location: Ethiopia — Coffea arabica is native to the Ethiopian highlands.
  • Topic: Coffee — Arabica is the species behind most specialty and café coffee.
  • Location: Yirgacheffe — Yirgacheffe lots are Coffea arabica sold under a place name.
  • Location: Mocha — Historic mocha shipments were Yemeni arabica through Al-Mukha.
  • Item: Jamaica Blue Mountain — Jamaica Blue Mountain is a branded highland arabica.
  • Location: Colombia — Colombia is a major washed-arabica origin on café menus.
  • Character: Kaldi — Kaldi is the folktale attached to the discovery of Arabica cherries.

What is Coffea arabica?

Coffea arabica, native to Ethiopian highlands, is the species of mocha, espresso blends, and third-wave single origins — milder and more terroir-sensitive than robusta.

Key threads lead to Ethiopia, Coffee, Yirgacheffe, Mocha, Jamaica Blue Mountain and Colombia.
